grades.reason: Table of contents only. It lists the LoongArch timer configuration (TCFG) and timer interrupt clearing (TICLR) sections, which points to relevant registers but gives no procedure.

grades.quote: Timer enable bit. Only when this bit is 1, the timer will perform countdown self decrement and set up the timing interrupt signal when it decrements to 0 value.
grades.reason: Describes how to configure the LoongArch timer through TCFG: enable bit, periodic mode and initial value. It does not cover acknowledging or clearing the interrupt, so it answers only the configure half.

grades.quote: A machine timer interrupt becomes pending whenever `mtime` contains a value greater than or equal to `mtimecmp` , treating the values as unsigned integers. The interrupt remains posted until `mtimecmp` becomes greater than `mtime` (typically as a result of writing `mtimecmp` ). The interrupt will only be taken if interrupts are enabled and the MTIE bit is set in the `mie` register.
grades.reason: Covers both halves for RISC-V. Software arms the timer by writing mtimecmp and enabling MTIE in mie. The interrupt stays pending until mtimecmp is raised above mtime, which is the acknowledge step. It also includes the RV32 write sequence and a note on spurious interrupts.

grades.quote: Clearing the timer interrupt is accomplished by the software via writing `1` to `CSR.TICLR.TI` .
grades.reason: Explains where the LoongArch timer interrupt comes from: it fires when the timer counts down to zero and is recorded in CSR.ESTA.IS[11]. It states that software clears it by writing 1 to CSR.TICLR.TI. This covers acknowledgement well but gives no configuration steps.
